title: MATH GAOKAO - 300
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Area Between a Line and a Parabola
questions.learningObjective: Find the area between \(y=x\) and \(y=x^2\) on the interval where they intersect.
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=x\) and \(y=x^2\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
x=x^2 \implies x(x-1)=0 \implies x=0 \text{ or } x=1.
\]
On \((0,1)\), the line \(y=x\) lies above the parabola \(y=x^2\). Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{1}(x-x^2)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{1}(x-x^2)\,dx
=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}
=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}
=\frac{1}{6}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points first, then integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.

questions.concept: Area Between a Parabola and a Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the area bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4x\).
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4x\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
x^2=4x \implies x(x-4)=0 \implies x=0 \text{ or } x=4.
\]
On \((0,4)\), the line \(y=4x\) lies above the parabola \(y=x^2\). Thus,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{4}(4x-x^2)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{4}(4x-x^2)\,dx
=\left[2x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{4}
=32-\frac{64}{3}
=\frac{32}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points and integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.

questions.concept: Total Area Between a Cubic Curve and the x-axis
questions.learningObjective: Compute the total area enclosed by \(y=x^3\) and the \(x\)-axis over a symmetric interval.
questions.question: Find the total area of the region bounded by \(y=x^3\) and the \(x\)-axis from \(x=-1\) to \(x=1\).
questions.explanation:
The curve crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=0\). On \([-1,0]\), \(x^3\le 0\), so the area is
\[
\int_{-1}^{0}(0-x^3)\,dx.
\]
On \([0,1]\), \(x^3\ge 0\), so the area is
\[
\int_{0}^{1}x^3\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{-1}^{0}(-x^3)\,dx
=\left[-\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-1}^{0}
=\frac{1}{4},
\]
and
\[
\int_{0}^{1}x^3\,dx
=\left[\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{0}^{1}
=\frac{1}{4}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\text{Total area}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
questions.hint: Split the integral at the point where the curve crosses the \(x\)-axis, then add the absolute areas.

questions.concept: Area Between an Exponential Curve and a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Find the area between \(y=e^x\) and \(y=1\) over a given interval.
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=e^x\), \(y=1\), and \(x=0\), \(x=1\).
questions.hint: Integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve over the given interval.

questions.concept: Area Between Sine and Cosine Curves
questions.learningObjective: Determine the area between \(y=\cos x\) and \(y=\sin x\) on the interval where they intersect.
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=\cos x\) and \(y=\sin x\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\).
questions.explanation:
On \(\left[0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right]\), \(\cos x\ge \sin x\). Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx
=\left[\sin x+\cos x\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}.
\]
At \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\):
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{4}+\cos\frac{\pi}{4}
=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
=\sqrt{2}.
\]
At \(x=0\):
\[
\sin 0+\cos 0=0+1=1.
\]
Thus,
\[
\text{Area}=\sqrt{2}-1.
\]
questions.hint: Identify which curve is on top on the given interval, then integrate the difference.

questions.concept: Area Between a Parabola and a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Find the area enclosed by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\).
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
x^2=4 \implies x=\pm 2.
\]
On \([-2,2]\), the line \(y=4\) lies above the parabola \(y=x^2\). Hence,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-x^2)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{-2}^{2}(4-x^2)\,dx
=\left[4x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}.
\]
At \(x=2\):
\[
8-\frac{8}{3}=\frac{16}{3}.
\]
At \(x=-2\):
\[
-8+\frac{8}{3}=-\frac{16}{3}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\frac{16}{3}-\left(-\frac{16}{3}\right)=\frac{32}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points and integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.

questions.learningObjective: Find the area between \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x^3\) on their interval of intersection.
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x^3\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
x^2=x^3 \implies x^2(1-x)=0 \implies x=0 \text{ or } x=1.
\]
On \((0,1)\), \(x^2>x^3\). Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{1}(x^2-x^3)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{1}(x^2-x^3)\,dx
=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_{0}^{1}
=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}
=\frac{1}{12}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points and determine which curve is on top between them.

questions.concept: Area Between a Square Root Curve and a Line
questions.learningObjective: Compute the area bounded by \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and \(y=x\).
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=\sqrt{x}\) and \(y=x\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
\sqrt{x}=x \implies x=x^2 \implies x(x-1)=0 \implies x=0 \text{ or } x=1.
\]
On \((0,1)\), \(\sqrt{x}>x\). Thus,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{1}(\sqrt{x}-x)\,dx
=\int_{0}^{1}(x^{1/2}-x)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{1}(x^{1/2}-x)\,dx
=\left[\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}
=\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}
=\frac{1}{6}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points and integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.

questions.concept: Area Between a Logarithmic Curve and the x-axis
questions.learningObjective: Find the area between \(y=\ln x\) and the \(x\)-axis over a given interval.
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=\ln x\), the \(x\)-axis, and the lines \(x=1\) and \(x=e\).
questions.explanation:
On \([1,e]\), \(\ln x\ge 0\). Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{1}^{e}\ln x\,dx.
\]
An antiderivative of \(\ln x\) is \(x\ln x-x\). Thus,
\[
\int_{1}^{e}\ln x\,dx
=\left[x\ln x-x\right]_{1}^{e}.
\]
At \(x=e\):
\[
e\ln e-e=e-e=0.
\]
At \(x=1\):
\[
1\ln 1-1=0-1=-1.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=0-(-1)=1.
\]
questions.hint: Recall the antiderivative of \(\ln x\) and evaluate it at the given limits.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the area bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x-x^2\).
questions.question: Find the area of the region bounded by \(y=x^2\) and \(y=2x-x^2\).
questions.explanation:
The curves intersect when
\[
x^2=2x-x^2 \implies 2x^2-2x=0 \implies 2x(x-1)=0 \implies x=0 \text{ or } x=1.
\]
On \((0,1)\), \(2x-x^2>x^2\). Therefore,
\[
\text{Area}=\int_{0}^{1}\bigl((2x-x^2)-x^2\bigr)\,dx
=\int_{0}^{1}(2x-2x^2)\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_{0}^{1}(2x-2x^2)\,dx
=\left[x^2-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}
=1-\frac{2}{3}
=\frac{1}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Find the intersection points and integrate the upper curve minus the lower curve.
